title: Decide whether a local dispatch through 'cloudflare-sandbox' is wanted, or say the name is cloud-host-only
description:
k4s made 'cloudflare-sandbox' an executor the Workflow-hosted reconciler dispatches through. A local `ticfac run-epic` whose profile names it is still refused: internal/cli/executor.go builds only local-subprocess and herdr.

That refusal is HONEST today — the Go build genuinely cannot reach a Cloudflare sandbox — but nothing states the boundary as a decision, so it reads as an omission. A reader cannot tell whether local dispatch through that name is unimplemented, unwanted, or forgotten.

Decide, and make the decision visible where someone would hit it:
 (a) a later item adds a Go executor that proxies dispatches through a deployment's factory, or
 (b) internal/cli's refusal says the name is honoured by the cloud host only.

Either way the refusal message should name the reason, so a profile that asks for it gets an answer rather than a list of what is supported.

Reported by k4s, run epic-ncv, finding 3541db4c.
acceptance_criteria: A local run whose profile names cloudflare-sandbox is refused with a message that states the boundary as a decision, or is dispatched through a proxying executor
